primary.concise_derived_summary: Sections 2.1–2.4 define a single-stock model with Brownian midprice, exponential terminal-wealth utility, inventory in shares, and quote-dependent Poisson executions. Inventory shifts reservation prices; quotes alter received order flow and subsequent inventory. Section 3.2 derives an approximate strategy under symmetric exponential intensities: its reservation center depends on signed inventory while its spread is inventory-independent under those assumptions. Section 3.3 evaluates simulated terminal P&L and inventory, not a sampled absolute-position-peak quantile or funding contract.

current_manuscript_claims_checked.exact_current_text: Dealers absorb customer order imbalances while managing inventory risk and scarce balance-sheet capacity. Inventory affects optimal dealer pricing (Ho and Stoll, 1981), FX dealing (Lyons, 1995), and observed inventory adjustment in dealership markets (Hansch, Naik and Viswanathan, 1998). Treasury intermediation likewise depends on dealer capacity (Duffie et al., 2023). A forecast of the maximum recorded position magnitude over a future horizon may support monitoring of the measured position: an endpoint can return toward its starting value after an intervening large position. Translating that monitoring signal into a particular margin or financing decision requires the corresponding contractual and balance-sheet inputs.

current_manuscript_claims_checked.exact_current_text: Stipulated shortfall/excess weights are not observed financing prices. Quotes, fills, hedges, book decomposition, collateral and cash flows would be required to map this passive envelope into an operational inventory, margin or funding policy. This study evaluates forecasts, not such interventions; Avellaneda and Stoikov (2008) provide a distinct active inventory-sensitive quoting framework.
